DELIVERABLE: Configure tool-result clearing to trigger only past a high token threshold and set clear_at_least to a large value (about 30k tokens) so each activation clears many old results at once; drop the clear-one-per-turn plan.
BOUNDARY: Each clear invalidates the cache from the cleared point onward, so clearing a single result every turn would turn the 85% hit rate into repeated misses; keep recent results and any active-debugging errors.
EVIDENCE: (1) Compare cache read hit rate and cached-token cost over 20 sessions with batched versus per-turn clearing; (2) task success unchanged.

DELIVERABLE: Reject per-turn clearing. Use a trigger threshold plus clear_at_least and clear in bulk.
BOUNDARY: Every clear rewrites the prefix after that point, so clearing each turn breaks the cache over and over.
EVIDENCE: Cache hit rate and cost per task before and after.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Clearing infrequently in large blocks: set the trigger well above the working set and a big minimum per activation; (2) never one-at-a-time.
BOUNDARY: The cache prefix after a cleared result is invalidated and must be recomputed, so each tiny incremental clear each turn costs more than it saves.
EVIDENCE: Measure cached-token share and latency per turn across both configurations.

DELIVERABLE: Clear in big batches rarely (clear_at_least high) instead of the proposed policy.
BOUNDARY: Cache prefix gets invalidated at every edit point, so per-turn single clears would bust it each turn.
EVIDENCE: Hit-rate delta over 30 sessions.

DELIVERABLE: Approve the proposal: clear the oldest tool result each turn once there are more than 20 results.
BOUNDARY: The stable system prompt keeps the cache warm.
EVIDENCE: Context size stays under 150k.

DELIVERABLE: Clear the oldest result on every turn after 20 results; occasional cache invalidation is acceptable.
BOUNDARY: Keep the last 5 results.
EVIDENCE: Track context size per turn.

DELIVERABLE: Send all 38 definitions unchanged on every request and restrict the 6 allowed tools per request with allowed_tools (or tool_choice), not by removing definitions.
BOUNDARY: Changing the tools block invalidates the cache for everything after it, including the 3k system prompt, so 90% hit rate would collapse for read-only sessions.
EVIDENCE: Hit rate for read-only versus normal sessions; a test that a write tool call is refused in read-only mode.

DELIVERABLE: Use tool_choice / allowed tools to limit the model to the 6 read-only tools; keep the tools array byte-identical.
BOUNDARY: A varying subset of definitions is a different prefix, so cache is missed on both mode variants.
EVIDENCE: Compare cached-token cost across modes.

DELIVERABLE: Do not rebuild the tools array. Constrain with allowed_tools instead of dropping 32 definitions.
BOUNDARY: Every request with a different tools block misses the prefix cache.
EVIDENCE: Hit rate stays near 90% in read-only mode.

DELIVERABLE: Keep the full stable tool list; pick the permitted ones through tool_choice per request.
BOUNDARY: Cache prefix stays identical.
EVIDENCE: Cache hit measurement.

DELIVERABLE: Build the tools array per request with only the 6 read-only definitions; it saves 7k tokens.
BOUNDARY: Normal sessions send all 38.
EVIDENCE: Token counts per request.

DELIVERABLE: Send the 6 read-only definitions in read-only mode and cache each variant separately.
BOUNDARY: Two prefixes to warm.
EVIDENCE: Hit rate per variant.

DELIVERABLE: Remove the self-estimate instruction. The harness reads token counts from each response's usage fields (or the token-counting API) and triggers compaction when usage reaches a measured_safe_limit chosen below the window limit.
BOUNDARY: The model does not receive a budget on this runtime, so it cannot be trusted to count; compaction late near the window loses user constraints, so set the limit from measured behavior.
EVIDENCE: Replay 10 sessions logging usage at trigger time versus the point where instruction-misses begin.

DELIVERABLE: Deterministic trigger in code: sum usage tokens from API responses; compaction fires at the measured safe limit, not at 80% of the window by guess.
BOUNDARY: Model self-reports are guesses; do not ask it to estimate.
EVIDENCE: Compare constraint retention after compaction before and after the change.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Harness-side counter from the token counting API; (2) compact at measured_safe_limit, which sits under the window limit; (3) delete the estimate line from the prompt.
BOUNDARY: Late compaction near the limit drops constraints.
EVIDENCE: Probe questions about original user constraints after each compaction.

DELIVERABLE: Use usage fields from the response; compaction at the safe limit measured on this workload.
BOUNDARY: Not an estimate by the model.
EVIDENCE: Missed-instruction rate.

DELIVERABLE: Tighten the prompt: tell the agent to estimate usage more carefully and compact at 70% instead.
BOUNDARY: The model keeps estimating itself.
EVIDENCE: Check whether sessions compact earlier.

DELIVERABLE: Raise the threshold to 90% of the window so compaction happens less often.
BOUNDARY: The model estimates usage.
EVIDENCE: Fewer compaction events.

DELIVERABLE: Replace 'ERR layer violation' with a custom lint whose message states the fix ('orders/ may not import billing/internal; import from billing/api instead'), so each failure injects the repair into the agent's context. Put the lint config and CI rules on a locked surface.

BOUNDARY: A bare error teaches nothing and the prompt text alone did not stop the agent.

BOUNDARY: Edits to rules need approval.

EVIDENCE: Watch for repeat violations.

EVIDENCE: Locked scores for the 11 ablations plus latency; results.tsv rows for each.

EVIDENCE: Ablation table with score and latency.

DELIVERABLE: (1) Leave-one-out pruning; (2) accept any removal that is no worse than the current score; (3) only then resume proposing changes.
